title: What Large Language Models Do Not Talk About: An Empirical Study of Moderation and Censorship Practices

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to generate biographies of political figures and measuring both 'hard censorship' (explicit refusals to answer) and 'soft censorship' (selective omission of widely acknowledged praises or accusations related to human rights, international crimes, and UN Sustainable Development Goals) using an LLM-as-a-judge.

Comparing the rates of hard and soft censorship across the generated descriptions based on the political figure's country or region of birth, specifically observing how models tailor censorship toward their provider's domestic audience.

Evaluating the differences in refusal rates and omission patterns when identical prompts about political figures are presented in the six official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish).
